p013-u002: The National University Student Robot Competition RoboMaster University Championship (RMUC) is initiated by DJI. Its core format is tactical combat between robots. Participating teams must independently design, develop and build multiple robots that meet the specifications, then field them as a robot team. During a seven-minute match, the two sides engage in tactical combat by operating their robots; destroying the opposing Base wins the match.
p013-u003: RMUC aims to cultivate outstanding young engineers and encourages participants to combine what they have learned with practical applications and continue to grow through participation.

p039-u001: The Dart Detection Module is located at the top of the Base and Outpost. It consists of a Dart Armor Module, Dart Detection Sensor and Dart Guidance Light.
p039-u002: The Dart Armor Module detects dart impacts. The Dart Detection Sensor detects the infrared beam emitted by the Dart Trigger Device. The system considers the module hit by a dart when the projection of the Dart Trigger Device onto the Dart Detection Module falls completely within the Dart Armor Module and the module detects both the infrared beam and an impact. If only an impact is detected, the system considers the module hit by a projectile. The Dart Guidance Light emits green visible light at a wavelength of 520 nm. When approximated as a point source, its luminous intensity is about 10 cd and its illuminated part is about 55 mm in diameter; it guides darts toward the target.
p039-u003: Even when the projection of the Dart Trigger Device onto the Dart Detection Module does not fall completely within the Dart Armor Module, there is still some probability that the Dart Detection Module will identify a hit successfully.

If the Referee System does not detect the killer, or the killer cannot gain Experience:
For projectile damage, the killer’s Level is treated as the Level corresponding to the average Experience of all surviving robots on the opposing side that can normally deal that type of projectile damage, and Experience is divided equally among those robots.
For non-projectile damage, Experience is divided equally among all surviving Infantry Robots on the opposing side at that time. Round the average to one decimal place.
If a robot becomes Defeated for a reason other than an Armor Module being attacked, becomes Abnormally Disconnected, or the Referee System cannot detect the killer, the killer is considered not found.
Example 1: A Level 2 Infantry Robot defeats an opposing Level 6 Infantry Robot. The killer gains 50 × 6 × (1 + (6 − 2) × 0.2) = 540 Experience.
Example 2: A Level 9 Red Infantry Robot is Defeated and no killer is detected. At this time, two Blue Infantry Robots survive with 1,250 and 4,000 total Experience. Their average Experience is 2,625, corresponding to Level 5. Each Blue Infantry Robot gains 50 × 9 × (1 + (9 − 5) × 0.2) / 2 = 405 Experience.

p113-u001: The functions of the Radar System include radar recognition and radar decoding of information waves, as follows:
p113-u003: The Radar can recognize the positions of both sides' Ground Robots and send the robots' coordinates to the Referee System server. Each Ground Robot has a "marked progress" P, with a value range from 0 (initial and minimum value) to 150 (maximum value). The Referee System updates P in real time according to the accuracy of the Radar's recognition: consecutive accurate marking makes P rise at an accelerating rate; conversely, consecutive erroneous marking or data interruption makes P decay at an accelerating rate. When P reaches certain thresholds, the corresponding target receives certain effects. In addition, by continuously marking to maintain the opponent's vulnerable state, the Radar can also unlock the "double vulnerability" effect.
p113-u004: Affected by the wireless environment at the match venue, or when the Positioning Module is covered over a large area, the coordinates detected by a robot's Positioning Module may, with small probability, exhibit intermittent or persistent drift.
p113-u007: d: recognition error, that is, the straight-line distance between the "coordinates sent by the Radar" and the "robot's actual planar coordinates", divided into three levels:
p113-u015: x: the influence value of the current marking (that is, the progress change amount), with an initial value of 0.
p113-u017: Judgment frequency: determined by the Radar's sending frequency.
p113-u019: Each time the Referee System receives Radar data, or the data is interrupted, x is updated first, then P is updated.
p113-u028: If the previous marking was accurate or semi-accurate, x=x+0.5; otherwise x=0.5
p113-u030: If the previous marking was erroneous/interrupted, x=x−0.8; otherwise x=−0.8
p113-u032: Each time the Referee System accumulates 0.5 seconds without receiving data, it is treated as triggering one "erroneous" judgment
p114-u000: Example: If one side's Radar continuously sends the coordinates of the opponent's Heavy Robot to the Referee System server at a frequency of 5Hz with 100% accuracy, then within 0 to 1 seconds, at 0.2-second intervals, the opponent Heavy Robot's marked progress is 1, 3, 6, 10, 15 respectively, and at second 3.0 the robot's marked progress reaches 120. After that, if the Radar sends the robot's coordinates to the Referee System server at a frequency of 5Hz with 0% accuracy, then within 3.0 to 4.0 seconds, at 0.2-second intervals, the robot's marked progress is 119.2,
p114-u001: 117.6, 115.2, 112, 108. After that, if the Radar does not send the Heavy Robot's coordinates for 1.0 consecutive seconds, then within 4.0 to 5.0 seconds the robot's marked progress will be 103.2, 97.6 (judged as two additional consecutive errors on top of the previous errors). After that, if the Radar sends the Heavy Robot's correct coordinates twice consecutively, the robot's marked progress will be 98.6, 100.6.

p114-u026: Double vulnerability mechanism: Each time the Radar accumulates 1 minute of making opponent robots vulnerable (when multiple robots are vulnerable at the same time, the time is not added up), it gains 1 opportunity to trigger "double vulnerability". The Radar can consume the opportunity by actively sending a command through the Referee System, which doubles all current vulnerability values originating from the Radar for 30 seconds. In each round, the Radar can trigger "double vulnerability" at most 2 times.
p114-u028: During the match, an official transmitting source will be placed on each side's Radar Base. This source transmits electromagnetic waves, including an information wave carrying the opposing team's information and an interference wave of a similar frequency band. The red side's broadcast source/interference source is placed on the red side's Radar Base and contains information about the blue team, and vice versa. Participating teams can build and install an antenna and a demodulation circuit on the Radar to decode and recognize the information wave and the interference wave, and to provide their own side with information and advantages.
p115-u000: The interference wave has three difficulty levels. Decoding difficulty rises with the difficulty level. Specific parameters will be released later.
p115-u001: The information wave will contain the following information about the opponent:
p115-u007: Remaining projectile allowance of each robot
p115-u009: Buffs currently held by each robot
p115-u015: Activation status of each of the opponent's Buff Points
p115-u018: For the specific communication protocol structure, see: "RoboMaster 2027 University Series Communication Protocol".
p115-u019: The interference wave contains no specific information, but contains a 6-character (alphanumeric combination) key customized by the opponent. The key is reset to a random value at the start of the round and whenever the difficulty of the corresponding side's interference wave changes.
p115-u020: At the start of a round, both sides' interference waves default to difficulty level 1.
p115-u021: The Radar can decode this key and send it to the event engine server. If decoding succeeds, the opponent's interference wave decoding difficulty subsequently rises by 1 level, that is, the difficulty of the interference source placed on one's own Radar Base rises by 1 level. When the opponent's interference wave difficulty is higher than one's own, the opponent's Radar will not produce vulnerability or accumulate "double vulnerability" progress against one's own robots, even if it marks them accurately.
p115-u023: The official matches of RMUC 2027 are divided into two stages: the group stage and the knockout stage. The group stage format is BO2 or BO3, and the knockout stage format is BO3 or BO5.
p115-u024: The outcome of a single round is determined item by item in the priority order of the following numbered list, until a final result is obtained:
p115-u026: When one side's Base is destroyed, the side with the higher remaining Base HP wins.
p115-u028: When the round time runs out, if neither side's Base is destroyed, the side with the higher cumulative control degree wins.
p115-u030: When the round time runs out, if neither side's Base is destroyed and the cumulative control degrees are equal, the side with the higher team attack damage wins.
p115-u032: When the round time runs out, if neither side's Base is destroyed, the cumulative control degrees are equal, and the team attack damage is equal, the side with the higher total team remaining HP wins.
p116-u001: If the winner cannot be determined under the above conditions, the round is considered a draw. In BO3 and BO5 matches, a draw immediately results in an additional round, until a winner is determined.

p134-u001: Multiple Restricted Zones are set up in the Battlefield. A Restricted Zone covers the ground and the vertical airspace above it. The extent of the Restricted Zones is shown in the figure below.
p134-u002: [1] Supply Restricted Zone [2] Base Restricted Zone [3] Assembly Restricted Zone [4] Dart Launching Station Restricted Zone
p134-u004: Robot interaction with Restricted Zones must follow the rules below, otherwise it is regarded as a violating entry into the Restricted Zone.
p134-u005: One-side Restricted Zone: only robots of the owning side may enter; all robots of the other side are prohibited from entering.
p134-u006: Shared Restricted Zone: all robots of both sides are prohibited from entering.
p135-u000: R56 Ground Robots must not enter the Base Restricted Zone in violation of the rules.

p135-u002: R57 Ground Robots must not enter the Supply Restricted Zone or Assembly Restricted Zone in violation of the rules.
p135-u003: If a robot is Defeated or ejected inside any Restricted Zone, the Referee may, depending on the situation on site, set the robot to a temporarily activated state and guide its Operator to operate the robot out of the Restricted Zone.
p135-u004: Violation penalty: warnings are issued to the violating robot according to the duration of stay and the impact of the violating behavior. The first Yellow Card Warning is issued when the violation duration exceeds 3 seconds, and then 1 Yellow Card Warning every 5 seconds until the violating robot is ejected. p135-u020: If any of the behaviors listed below occurs during the competition, it is judged a serious violation. For serious violations, the RMOC will disqualify the violating party at most from the competition.
p136-u000: If the behavior violates local laws and regulations, the RMOC will cooperate with the relevant authorities in pursuing the legal liability of the offender.
p137-u001: There may be some delay in the Referee's manual penalties and handling of abnormal situations. If this has a major impact on the match result, the Chief Referee will determine the final handling according to the actual situation.
p137-u002: If any of the following abnormal situations occurs, it will be handled in the corresponding way, and neither team may object. The handling is as follows:
p137-u004: When a serious safety hazard or abnormal condition occurs, for example battery combustion or explosion, venue power outage, high-pressure gas cylinder explosion or conflict among personnel on the field, after the Head Referee finds and confirms it, the Head Referee will notify both Operators and eject all robots through the Referee System, the result of that round is void, and the round is restarted after the hazard or abnormal condition is cleared. The RMOC will handle safety problems first and protect the robots as far as possible, but cannot guarantee that robots will not be affected at all; any loss or impact caused by safety handling is borne by the participating team.
p137-u006: During the match, if non-critical props in the Battlefield are damaged, for example damaged floor mat, damaged field Light Indicators or damaged Base lighting effects, which do not affect the fairness of the match, the match proceeds normally.
p137-u008: During the match, if abnormal robot Armor Module lighting effects or Light Indicator effects, damaged Armor Modules or similar situations occur, the match proceeds normally.
p137-u010: During the match, if critical official equipment or props malfunction or are structurally damaged in a way that affects the fairness of the match, for example the on-site network is abnormal and causes robots to go offline, the Buff is not triggered after hitting the Power Rune, or the field prop mechanisms cannot operate normally, the Referee will handle such faults manually through the Referee System. If the fault cannot be handled manually, the Referee will notify both Operators and eject all robots, the round ends immediately and its result is void. After the problem is resolved, the round is restarted.
p137-u012: During the match, if critical official equipment or props malfunction or are structurally damaged in a way that affects the fairness of the match, and the Head Referee does not confirm and end the round in time, so that a round that should have ended continues and produces a win/loss result, then within 5 minutes after the match ends, once verified by the Chief Referee, the result of that round is void and the round must be replayed.
p137-u014: If a serious violation that clearly triggers a Loss by forfeit penalty occurs but the Head Referee does not confirm and enforce it in time, then within 5 minutes after the match ends, once verified by the Chief Referee, the result of that round is void and an additional Loss by forfeit penalty is imposed on the violating party.
p137-u016: During the match, if a situation that may affect the fairness of the match occurs, within 5 minutes after the match ends the Chief Referee will inform both team captains and suspend the result confirmation process, and within the following 60 minutes will verify the situation and inform both team captains of the final handling. Neither team may object to the handling result.
p138-u001: Each participating team has 1 Appeal opportunity each in the Regional Competition, the Revival Tournament and the Final Tournament; they cannot be combined. If the Appeal succeeds, the Appeal opportunity is retained; otherwise 1 Appeal opportunity is consumed. When no Appeal opportunity remains, the arbitration committee will no longer accept any Appeal from that team. After an Appeal is accepted, the arbitration committee arbitrates on the Appeal materials and related evidence, and the Chief Referee informs both parties of the Appeal result on behalf of the arbitration committee; the arbitration committee has the final right of interpretation of the Appeal result.
p138-u002: The following cannot be used as grounds for an Appeal:
p138-u004: Verbal warnings, Yellow Card Warnings and Red Card Warnings in violation penalties.
p138-u006: The type and procedure of initiating a technical pause.
p138-u008: "Normal battle damage" occurring on the Referee System onboard unit.
p138-u009: An Appeal cannot be initiated after signing the result confirmation form or more than 5 minutes after a match ends.
p139-u001: A participating team that needs to make an Appeal should follow this procedure:
p139-u002: Within 5 minutes after the match ends (as recorded on the result confirmation form), in the group stage a team may appeal all rounds in the match, and in the knockout stage the team that did not win may appeal the rounds of the match that it did not win. The Appeal is raised by the team captain at the result confirmation desk; confirming the submission starts the Appeal procedure and consumes the Appeal opportunity. After the result confirmation form has been signed, or 5 minutes after the match ends, the arbitration committee no longer accepts Appeals. Appeals are not allowed before or during the match.
p139-u005: If the Appeal reason involves the robots of both sides, the arbitration committee has the right to isolate the relevant robots; robots isolated for inspection will be returned no later than together with the Appeal result.
p139-u006: After the Appeal form is provided, the appealing team captain must fill in the Appeal form in detail at the result confirmation desk and sign and submit it within 10 minutes. While filling in the Appeal form, in addition to the captain, at most 2 field personnel are allowed to assist. The arbitration committee arbitrates only on the "Appeal reason" part of the Appeal form, which the appealing party may not modify or supplement afterwards. If the form is not signed and submitted within 10 minutes, it is regarded as having no "Appeal reason", the subsequent procedure is skipped, and the Appeal result is regarded as "original match result upheld".
p139-u007: Team fills in the Appeal form and signs to confirm.
p139-u008: If either party needs to collect Appeal materials, it must submit them to the Chief Referee within 30 minutes after the Appeal is accepted, with the time and place of submission agreed in advance, and the Appeal materials must be explained in detail at submission.
p139-u009: Team collects evidence or defense materials.
p139-u010: After the Appeal material submission period expires, the arbitration committee does not accept new materials. If neither party needs to collect Appeal materials, the arbitration committee has already established sufficient evidence, or the Appeal reason filled in by the appealing party cannot be used as grounds for an Appeal, the procedure may proceed directly to the next step.
p139-u011: After the arbitration committee reaches a ruling based on the relevant evidence, it notifies both team captains to come to the arbitration room, and the basis of the ruling is shown and the Appeal result announced in this step. Both parties must arrive at the arbitration room within 10 minutes after the arbitration committee's notice. This step allows in-person participation only. Each party may have no more than 3 members present, and the members present may only be official team members or advisors. If either party is absent, the absent party is regarded as having automatically waived participation. If the appealing party's Appeal reason is clearly inconsistent with the facts or is a reason that cannot be used as grounds for an Appeal, the arbitration committee may explain the situation only to the appealing party and uphold the original match result. When the representatives of both parties accept the Appeal result, or the arbitration committee considers that the necessary communication has been completed, the procedure moves to the next step.
p139-u012: Appeal result is announced to both parties.
p139-u013: The arbitration committee gives the Appeal result on the Appeal form, and 1 of the members of each party in the arbitration room must sign the Appeal form as representative; signing means acknowledging the Appeal result, and neither party may object to the Appeal result afterwards. If the form is not signed within 5 minutes after the Appeal result is given, the arbitration result is regarded as acknowledged. If the appealing party's Appeal reason is clearly inconsistent with the facts or is a reason that cannot be used as grounds for an Appeal, the arbitration committee explains the situation to the appealing party and upholds the original match result; the appealed party does not need to sign and is regarded as having acknowledged the Appeal result.
p139-u015: If a round is replayed because the Appeal arbitration result was "both sides replay", then after the replayed round ends, teams that still have an Appeal opportunity may appeal the replayed round. In this case, if the original appealing party appeals again (called a "Continued Appeal"), because it seriously affects the schedule, the original appealing party's Appeal opportunity is consumed whether or not the Appeal succeeds.
p139-u019: Each file in the Appeal materials submitted by a participating team must not exceed 500MB, and there must be no more than 10 files.
p140-u001: Appeal results include: original match result upheld, appealed party Loss by forfeit, and both sides replay. After the arbitration committee confirms the Appeal result, neither party may object to it.
p140-u003: Appeal succeeds: appealed party Loss by forfeit, or both sides replay.
p140-u005: Appeal fails: original match result upheld.
p140-u006: If the result announced in the arbitration communication step is both sides replay, but neither side accepts the replay, the Appeal is regarded as failed and the original match result is upheld.
p140-u008: Where it does not affect the overall schedule, replays are in principle scheduled after all matches of the day end, subject to actual circumstances.
p140-u010: The replay procedure is the same as the regular schedule procedure, and both sides must play at the time specified by the RMOC and comply with the relevant regulations.
p140-u011: If the Appealed round affects the win/loss outcome of the match, the match outcome must be re-determined.
p140-u012: Example: A BO3 match ends 1:2, with Red winning the first round and Blue winning the second and third rounds. After the match, Red appeals the second round and the Appeal result is both sides replay. If Red wins the replayed round, the final match result is 2:0; if Blue wins the replayed round, the final match result is 1:2.
p141-u001: This season there will be no separate Sentry mapping session.
p141-u003: Pre-Inspection is an inspection session set before the formal Pre-Match Inspection, intended to help participating teams find and resolve problems with their robots in advance. During Pre-Inspection and adaptive training, the RMOC will do its best to help teams troubleshoot and handle robot faults, but the Pre-Inspection result is not equivalent to the formal match Pre-Match Inspection result; if a robot is found at the formal Pre-Match Inspection not to meet the passing criteria, it still may not take the field.
p141-u004: Unique identifier registration can only be done during Pre-Inspection; after Pre-Inspection ends, only replacement re-registration of robots whose unique identifiers have already been registered is allowed.
p141-u005: If a team needs to repair or replace a part that carries a unique identifier, it must apply to the RMOC to report it and re-register and re-mark it. Each team may initiate at most 6 such reports in the same competition region; replacing a part that carries a unique identifier without reporting it causes the robot to lose its eligibility to take the field.
p141-u007: Non-emergency reporting method: if the team's next match is more than 2 hours away, or it is outside the RMOC's working hours, the team may replace the relevant parts itself and, in [Robot Unique Identifier Re-registration], submit detailed photos of the robot before and after the replacement or a full video of the replacement process, book an inspection time through the same link, and arrive at the second Pre-Match Inspection area at the agreed time, where dedicated RMOC staff will review it. Robots that pass the review will receive their unique identifiers again.
p141-u009: Emergency reporting method: if the team's next match is less than 2 hours away and it is within the RMOC's working hours, the team should contact the Referee at the second Pre-Match Inspection area to report an emergency repair. After confirmation, RMOC staff will accompany the team to the team preparation area and supervise the whole repair process. In this case, the robot may pass Pre-Match Inspection and take part in this match without all unique identifiers being completed, but after the team's next match ends, the robot must be moved to the second Pre-Match Inspection area for a second review and have all unique identifiers completed.
p141-u011: Prop training provides field props and wooden structures similar to those used in the formal match for participating teams to test with. Passing Pre-Match Inspection is not required before training; teams must make sure their robots' Referee System works properly, and if the on-site Referee System fails, the related time counts toward that team's training time.
p141-u013: Each team must wait in the waiting area 20 minutes in advance; for teams that do not arrive on time, training time is still counted as normal and is not extended. Each team has two training sessions in total, each 30 minutes (including entering and leaving the field). The first session is arranged by the RMOC and the second is booked by the team itself; enter and leave strictly according to the time slots, and do not occupy other teams' training time.
p141-u015: Each team may send at most 12 people into the training area, and entrants must wear safety goggles. The RMOC provides only 2 Operator computers for the video transmission channel; if more robot player-side devices need to be connected, teams may bring their own computers, but these must not be connected to the competition network.
p142-u001: The RMOC provides only Movable Props for testing and does not provide 17mm or 42mm projectiles; teams must bring their own if testing requires them. When testing with 42mm projectiles, take care to avoid actively hitting the Power Rune. Because of venue limitations, the training area may be affected by ambient light, and teams must adapt on their own. If a team does not obey the on-site Referee or commits other violations, its prop training eligibility will be revoked and it will be asked to leave immediately; in serious cases its adaptive training eligibility is also revoked.
p142-u003: Adaptive training is a debugging and acclimatization opportunity for participating teams before the formal matches. Its main purposes include:
p142-u005: Become familiar with the competition environment and procedures.
p142-u007: Test and adjust robot status and strategy.
p142-u010: The training schedule is tight and mainly for debugging; absent a major official equipment failure, training is not paused by default.
p142-u012: If the Referee System (onboard unit) is abnormal, the RMOC may grant an official technical pause of at most 2 minutes to handle the fault; the pause duration counts toward the total adaptive training time.
p142-u014: No team technical pause opportunity is provided during adaptive training.
p142-u015: Rules for the free debugging stage:
p142-u017: When testing projectile launching, a team may apply to the Referee to borrow a projectile clearing bag and may launch only into the clearing bag.
p142-u019: During the free debugging stage the match stage status is "Not Started"; teams must adapt to and become familiar with the switching and requirements of the match stages themselves.
p142-u022: Robots that did not pass Pre-Match Inspection on time or that have safety hazards may not take part in adaptive training.
p142-u024: Robots that failed Pre-Match Inspection because they seriously do not meet the inspection standards are allowed to take part only in the free debugging stage of adaptive training.
p142-u026: The number of robots taking part in adaptive training must not exceed the maximum robot lineup limit specified for each event.
